column1: # Vercel per-project registry (DIC-1401).
# Maps each Vercel project's TRUSTED runtime identity (project id or
# production URL — both are per-PROJECT properties Vercel injects at build
# time, NOT values that travel with the branch being built) to the branch
# that project is contracted to serve as its Production deployment.
# Why this file exists: the previous round bound the guard to
# EXPECTED_VERCEL_BRANCH which was declared inside each branch's own
# vercel.json. That declaration travels with the branch, so if a Vercel
# project is misconfigured (or a dashboard setting drifts) to build the wrong
# branch, the branch's own vercel.json says "expected=<that same branch>"
# and the guard trivially matches. This registry defeats that: the identity
# used for lookup (VERCEL_PROJECT_ID or VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL) is a
# per-project property that stays with the PROJECT, whichever branch is
# checked out. The registry file is committed to every branch, so its
# contents are identical regardless of which branch is being built.
# Adding an entry: prefer project_id (immutable UUID assigned by Vercel).
# production_url is accepted as a fallback for projects whose id has not
# been populated yet (DIC-1399 unblocked the project ids upstream but the
# workspace secret was previously stale). Both fallback and canonical
# domains for each project should be listed, since Vercel returns whichever
# domain the dashboard has marked as the primary Production domain.
# Format: identity_kind<TAB>identity_value<TAB>allowed_branch<TAB>label
#   identity_kind ∈ { project_id, production_url }
#   identity_value ∈ literal string compared with the corresponding env var
#   allowed_branch ∈ branch this project is allowed to build as Production
#   label ∈ human-readable Vercel project name / note
